A covered upper register and rounded main release, preserving the shorter edge.

The upper choir enters later and remains lighter; pressure adds effort and upper color without moving the vowel bands with the played pitch. A gently open body, a defined attack and a clean key release.

program.name: Harp
program.description: A finger-plucked harp string excites a rounded soundboard response with a broad, softly notched upper spectrum. The short contact rank shares the string's pitch, then yields to a long lower aftersound. Soft arpeggios retain their gentler attack and can ring across key releases.

program.name: Koto
program.description: A near-bridge plectrum opens a bright notched string spectrum over the koto's long-board response. A quiet short contact rank shares the played pitch; upper string modes soften before the ringing body. Restrained initial settling leaves the ribbon available for deliberate bends.

program.name: Banjo
program.description: A sharp string pluck excites the banjo's membrane-and-bridge response, with a strong low-mid body and a dry bright edge. Fast losses around the head resonance let the sound clear between picked notes; the brief contact rank adds no unrelated clavichord or held oscillator buzz.

program.name: Kalimba
program.description: A thumb-plucked supported tine gives a rounded fundamental and a brief nonharmonic ping, distinct from an electric-piano pickup. Both ranks share the played pitch; the brighter contact fades first while the lower tine continues ringing after key release.

program.name: Tubular Bells
program.description: A struck tube carries a weak low spectrum and a bright octave nominal, with the near 2:3:4 upper group suggesting the played pitch. The separate hard contact shares the same tube tuning, then clears to leave its independently decaying metal modes.

program.name: Music Box
program.description: A small plucked comb tooth rings with a clear high pitch and sparse upper resonances near 6.27 times its fundamental. A short same-pitch contact glint lights the attack; the bright overtones fade into the simple mechanical ringing tail.

program.name: Gong
program.description: A low mallet thud opens into a dense, irregular set of plate modes. Delayed upper resonances bloom after the impact, then lose energy at different rates; the same tuned plate supplies the strike and the lingering, shifting aftersound.

program.name: Temple Bell
program.description: A deep struck shell rings with stable close mode pairs and slow metallic beating. Widely separated upper resonances recede from the initial clang, leaving a calm low aftersound; the brief hard contact and the long body share one shell pitch.

program.name: Xylophone
program.description: A hard high-register wooden bar carries a strong third harmonic, with a bright opening and compact pitched decay. Fast independent losses remove the upper knock early, keeping repeated notes dry and distinct.

program.name: Steel Drum
program.description: A struck steel shell carries a tuned octave and twelfth above the fundamental. A rounded mallet contact gives way to independently fading shell modes; each note retains its pitched center without a fixed carrier.

program.name: Agogo
program.description: A small hollow bell opens with a hard contact and several widely spaced metal resonances. Its compact shell damps quickly for repeated strokes; a short same-pitch upper knock adds definition to each crisp metal hit.

program.name: Distant Keys 113
program.description: A bright hammered steel-string spectrum rings in two courses. Rapidly fading high partials and small pitch beating give way to a clearer lower body; the shorter upper course emphasizes hard mallet strokes. A subdued upper edge over a longer body ending; characteristic body detail remains present.

program.name: Dulcimer
program.description: A bright hammered steel-string spectrum rings in two courses. Rapidly fading high partials and small pitch beating give way to a clearer lower body; the shorter upper course emphasizes hard mallet strokes.

program.name: Dulcimer Pluck
program.description: A firm steel-string pluck has a bright short octave course and a longer lower body. Upper modes lose energy independently, leaving a clear ringing string after the plectrum edge has faded.
